queries.query_text: inosine short-chain fatty acids LC-MS/MS tumor microenvironment serum quantification method validation

What are the specific analytical protocols, such as LC-MS/MS parameters and sample processing standards, for quantifying absolute physiological concentrations of inosine and short-chain fatty acids in human tumor microenvironments or serum?

still_missing: This study does not provide a measurement protocol for inosine. It does not address sample preparation or quantification specifically for tumor microenvironment (TME) tissue, focusing only on serum and feces. The reference ranges cited are from a general metabolomics database (HMDB) rather than a cancer-specific consensus statement or standardized reference range for tumor patients. The success criterion regarding 'consensus statements' or 'reference ranges' for cancer contexts remains unmet.
usable_content: This study provides a detailed Basic Protocol 1 for quantifying 14 short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in human serum and feces using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). It specifies alkaline extraction (pH > 7) using sodium hydroxide, derivatization with MTBSTFA at 60 °C, and specific GC-MS parameters (e.g., oven temperature program, ion source settings). It includes a table of 14 SCFA standards with retention times and quantification masses. It references the Human Metabolomics Database (HMDB) for normal concentration ranges of acetic acid in human blood (26.8 to 64.2 μM). It outlines calibration curve requirements (R2 ≥ 0.95) and sample storage conditions (−80 °C for long-term). 该研究建立并验证了一种用于生物样本（牛血清和牛奶）中短链脂肪酸（SCFA）绝对定量的 LC-MS 方法。核心方案包括使用 3-硝基苯肼（3-NPH）进行衍生化，结合反相液相色谱 - 质谱（RP-LC-MS）分析。方法学验证显示其具有高灵敏度（大多数分析物 LOD ≤ 0.1 µmol/L）、准确性（加标回收率 84–115%）和重现性（RSD < 7%）。该研究证明了在复杂生物基质（含脂质干扰）中检测挥发性 SCFA 的技术可行性，并提供了具体的衍生化反应条件（30°C, 30 min）和色谱分离参数。 This study describes the application of UHPLC-MS/MS to quantify short-chain fatty acids (specifically butyrate) in mouse plasma and feces, and GC-MS for tumor tissue, reporting measurable concentration changes linked to anti-PD-L1 therapy outcomes in a syngeneic NKTCL mouse model.
